# Template: bayes_tree
A natural-frequency tree, the Gigerenzer-style antidote to base-rate neglect: a population box at the top splits into sick/healthy by prevalence, each splits again by the test's sensitivity and specificity, every branch labeled with counts of PEOPLE (never bare probabilities), and a punchline box computes the positive predictive value — how few of the positives are actually sick. Choose this scene for ANY request about Bayes' theorem or Bayesian updating with tests, screening or diagnostic test accuracy, false positives, base rates, positive predictive value, or "the test is 90% accurate, I tested positive — do I have it?".
Parameter schema:
{
 "type": "object",
 "properties": {
  "population": {
   "type": "integer",
   "description": "How many people the tree follows, 100-100000 (default 1000)."
  },
  "prevalence": {
   "type": "number",
   "description": "Base rate of the condition, 0.0001-0.5 (default 0.01)."
  },
  "sensitivity": {
   "type": "number",
   "description": "P(test positive | sick), 0.5-1 (default 0.9)."
  },
  "specificity": {
   "type": "number",
   "description": "P(test negative | healthy), 0.5-1 (default 0.91)."
  },
  "condition": {
   "type": "string",
   "description": "Short name of the condition, e.g. \"the disease\" (default)."
  },
  "title": {
   "type": "string"
  }
 }
}
Element ids your commands can reference:
- root: the population box at the top
- sick: the sick branch box (healthy likewise)
- healthy: the healthy branch box
- tp: true positives box (sick, test +); fn / fp / tn likewise
- fn: false negatives (sick, test −)
- fp: false positives (healthy, test +) — the deceivers
- tn: true negatives (healthy, test −)
- edge_sick: branch arrow with its probability label (edge_healthy, edge_tp, edge_fn, edge_fp, edge_tn likewise)
- edge_healthy: branch to the healthy box
- edge_tp: branch to true positives
- edge_fn: branch to false negatives
- edge_fp: branch to false positives
- edge_tn: branch to true negatives
- ppv_box: the punchline box computing P(sick | positive)
- title: figure title, when set
Examples:
Request: "I tested positive on a 90 percent accurate screening test. What are the chances I'm sick?" → params: {"title":"One positive test"}
Request: "Draw a natural frequency tree for a rare disease and a good test." → params: {"prevalence":0.001,"sensitivity":0.95,"specificity":0.95,"title":"Rare disease, good test"}

In YAML: `template: bayes_tree` and `params:` per the schema above; commands name the element ids above.
